dominantPattern_narrative:
The dominant failure pattern (4 of 7, ~57%) is SEMANTIC_COMPILATION: the compiler retrieved the correct source section but either (a) silently dropped an entire required defined term from an otherwise-successfully-compiled 1.01 definitions batch (RGT-C-008 'Final Maturity Date', RGT-C-029 'Collateral Documents', both CRITICAL/MATERIAL and both housed in the same doc-a 1.01 candidate that DID correctly extract a dozen other definitions from the same section), (b) extracted only one of several interlinked definitions the claim requires (RGT-C-030, 2 of 3 linked terms missing), or (c) truncated a definition's text with an internal ellipsis at exactly the point containing a required qualifier, externalizing the day-count into an opaque unstructured input instead (RGT-C-022). None of these are wholesale extraction failures -- the housing candidate almost always got most of the section right -- they are narrower 'compiled some but not all of the content this specific claim needs' gaps. The second pattern (2 of 7, ~29%), bucketed OTHER, is a sampling-budget artifact rather than a pipeline-layer defect: both RGT-C-014 and RGT-C-058 are claims whose full proposition spans multiple sections/sub-clauses, and only some of the needed sections were selected into the 38-candidate compile budget (doc-a 2.04(a) was never compiled at all for RGT-C-014; only 2 of 5 lettered conditions precedent were compiled for RGT-C-058). Given a larger compile budget these would likely resolve on their own without any compiler or verifier fix. The remaining 1 claim (RGT-C-018) is a genuine STRUCTURAL_INDEX ambiguity: two physical structural nodes both normalize to 'Section 2.03' (a table-of-contents entry and the real heading) with no nodeId supplied to disambiguate, so getOperativeProvision correctly refused to guess and returned only the TOC fragment. 

Crucially, VERIFICATION performed exactly as it should have across all 7: every housing candidate for every one of these 7 NO_CREDIT claims carried a non-confident status (MATERIAL_DISCREPANCY, VERIFICATION_INCOMPLETE, or VERIFICATION_FAILED), and in at least one case (RGT-C-022) verification independently named the exact defect (the dropped 'zero if there is no such period' day-count branch) via a specific finding. Zero of the 7 are silent, confidently-wrong outputs -- dangerousSilentOmissionCount is 0 across all 117 GT claims. So the story of this run's compilation failures is not 'verification is asleep at the wheel'; it is 'the semantic compiler partially under-extracts definition-heavy sections and multi-clause claims, but the safety net (verification flagging non-confident status, plus the compiler's own sufficiency/requiredReview markers) reliably catches it before it would ever reach a human as a false negative.' The much larger practical constraint on this run's usefulness is not compilation or verification quality at all -- it is the 38-of-755 compile-budget cap itself: 97 of 117 GT claims (83%) were never compiled simply because the AI-Gateway cost ceiling stopped the run after 38 candidates, even though discovery correctly located the right section for the vast majority of them (materialCovenantBearingSectionRecall = 108/113 = 95.6% using the full 887-candidate discovery population).
